utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, will you please call the case?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour, case number IT-99-37-PT, the Prosecutor versus Nikola Sainovic and Dragoljub Ojdanic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honour for the Prosecution, it's the Prosecutor Madam Carla Del Ponte, my learned colleague, Julia Baly and myself Milbert Shin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Toma Fila and Zoran Jovanovic for the accused Sainovic, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Tomislav Visnjic and Vojislav Selezan, council for General Ojdanic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, this is the first Status Conference in this case, the purpose of which is to ensure the expeditious preparation of the case for trial and to review the status of the case and to allow the Defence the opportunity to raise any issues relating to the case. As Judge May is the -- the Pre-Trial Judge in this case, is away now, I'm presiding over this Status Conference in my capacity as a member of Trial Chamber III. I think there are several matters to consider during this conference, which include the issue of the indictment, disclosure, and other pending motions. However, the -- as the parties may have been already informed, the hearing on the provisional release for both of the accused has been set to take place on Monday, quarter past two, so that matter will be heard at that time. So let me start with the issue of the indictment. The accused are charged on the same indictment, that Mr. Milosevic is currently being tried upon, and the Prosecution is -- has passed the halfway and almost reaching the final stage of presenting its case in the Kosovo aspect of that trial. So how does the Prosecution propose to deal with the trial of these accused? So does the indictment have to be separated? Could you comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the position of the Prosecutor, the Prosecution is that we will most likely not be seeking joinder of these accused with the accused Milosevic. Rather, these accused will be tried separately. The Prosecution will review the position and if appropriate make the relevant filings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. If the Prosecution could file the submission in writing within some -- a week from now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Another matter regarding the indictment is concerned with another co-accused, Mr. Stojiljkovic, who I understand has died some time in April and I wonder if the Prosecution will file a submission regarding that matter, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour it's the understanding of the Prosecution as well that Mr. Stojiljkovic has passed away. The Prosecution will seek to obtain a death certificate and will make the appropriate filings thereafter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We will wait for that. Then the next matter will be about the disclosure. This Chamber has now issued some decisions granting protective measures in respect of witnesses whose statements are required to be disclosed by the Prosecution under Rule 66(A)(i) and ordering the Defence not to disclose to the public supporting materials, the identities of the witnesses, and any evidence disclosed to the accused under Rule 66(A)(i). I'd like to ask the Prosecution whether the material supporting the indictment, and confirmation that it has been disclosed to the Defence pursuant to the Rule 66(A)(i).

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the disclosure of materials pursuant to Rule 66(A)(i) is now complete and has been complete as of the 19th of June, 2002. If I could just briefly summarise the history of that, the 66(A)(i) disclosure began on May 6 for the accused Sainovic and on May 2nd for the accused Ojdanic. Thereafter, as the Prosecutor had indicated during the initial appearances, the Prosecution had filed these motions seeking an order of non-disclosure to the public of supporting materials and also an order seeking the extension of the protective measures that were granted in the Milosevic case. After receiving an order -- decision from the Trial Chamber on those motions on the 7th of June, Prosecution then continued to disclose pursuant to Rule 66(A)(i) and completed, as I indicated on the 19th of June. The total binders are, I believe, 12 binders. The Prosecutor may have indicated there were approximately 14 binders in the -- during the initial appearances but this is essentially the same material with the sake of convenience collated the materials in more than one binder on two occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. My understanding is that talks about the -- regarding the Rule 86 disclosures going on. So is there anything to raise regarding that matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The Prosecution met with Defence counsel yesterday to discuss, among other things, the Rule 68 disclosure as well as some issues relating to translation and particularly with the case, the accused Ojdanic, the Rule 66(B) disclosure, the reciprocal disclosure the corresponding part of which is Rule 67(C), at the meeting yesterday and I believe the -- Your Honour may have received a copy draft copy of the minutes, the counsel for the accused who have an opportunity to file something indicate being their comments, whether they agree with that draft or not in due course. Among the topics discussed were, as I said, the Rule 68 obligations and the reciprocal disclosure. If I could just summarise what, in brief, the areas that were covered, the Prosecution, in short, explained the process by which Rule 68 disclosure has been taking place in the Milosevic case. We understand of course that there are obvious differences between the Milosevic case and the case against these two accused, but we thought that that may be useful guide. We explained basically the process and the process in short is this: That we, the Prosecution, have identified certain searches that need to be made, first of all, and secondly we've gone to a sift of the document that is have been produced as a result of the searches through the holdings of the Prosecution. And thirdly we have reviewed those materials for the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. applicability of Rule 68. We have made available to Defence counsel examples of the searches that we've made. We have provided them a list of the major collections within the holdings of the Prosecution. And by that I mean major collections of documents, and we've also provided them with two versions of the accused Ojdanic's letter of April, I believe April 26, seeking discovery of various materials. These two charts recast -- excuse me, I've been indicated to slow down and I will do so. These two charts, basically take the letter of General Ojdanic and break it down into separate categories within which we will endeavour to fulfil our discovery obligations. Basically, the Prosecution explained that as with the Milosevic case, this type of search is potentially inefficient and time consuming process, and therefore, as with the Milosevic case, the Prosecution has invited the Defence counsel to provide any input or any suggestions they would have as to the means by way we are going about this, including suggestions on search parameters or any other methods by which we could make this process more efficient for all parties concerned. I think that may be all I had to say about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, the next matter will be some pending motions, but apart from the motion for provisional release, I noticed that there were two motions from Ojdanic's counsel regarding the access to the documents of Court and regarding the ex parte filings from the Prosecution but the Court decisions have already been made. So are there any matters which you would like to raise at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, we have satisfied with the decision and in view of the fact that this is a parallel process which will take place between the OTP and the registry, we shall wait for the results. After that, we will retain the right, as mentioned in the decision, to apply to the Chamber should we have any further issues to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Whether there are some -- any matters which the Prosecution wish to raise at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Perhaps with the exception that in connection with reciprocal disclosure, for the accused Mr. Ojdanic, the Prosecution should be in a position in late July or early August to begin that disclosure, in particular in reference to Mr. Ojdanic's letter of April 26th, again I believe that's the correct date, we should be in a position to begin disclosure on paragraphs 3 (B), (F) and (G). Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have anything to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, only with respect to the evidence disclosed so far. For the record, the Defence of General Ojdanic received the materials on the 2nd of May, and on the 13th, 18th and 19th of June. We wish to confirm what the Prosecution has said, that the material has been disclosed in its entirety. In relation to Rule 68, it is our understanding that it is the duty of the Prosecutor, which is equally important, that is, it is just as important for the Prosecution to look for exculpatory material as for incriminating material. We shall of course try to assist and facilitate this process, but we expect the full cooperation of the Prosecution, because it is up to them, in fact, to do this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Just two points on that, Your Honour. As my learned counsel has correctly pointed out, it is ultimately with regards to Rule 68 the obligation, of course, that the Prosecution to make that disclosure. And we would appreciates the assistance of Defence counsel in that regard. With regard briefly on the Rule 66(A)(1) disclosure just to reiterate that the Prosecution had at one point suspended disclosure under that rule while it had awaited the rulings of the Trial Chamber on the two motions that we had filed, of which I had spoken previously. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That includes the corrigendum regarding K20.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The final matter I'd like to raise -- yes, Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have a different view of the way Rule 68 should be applied and I believe that this is a little premature. On the 19th, we received two plus ten binders. I would first have to study the incriminating material in order to see what kind of material we should look for under Rule 68. Therefore I reserve the right after I have studied the material, if I am permitted to say something about this issue at some future Status Conference, to do so, because at present there is nothing I can do but agree with my colleagues. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will bear that in mind. Yes, Mr. Shin?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, just one additional note I've been informed by my colleague, Ms. Graham, that there may have been some confusion in our disclosure of Rule 66(A)(1) material. There may be one additional document it that we have not disclosed but I'll look into it and take care of the matter accordingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you Mr. Shin. The final matter is the so-called Rule 65 ter conference. It is the practice of this Trial Chamber that regular Pre-Trial Conferences are held with the Senior Legal Officer of the Chamber to expedite the preparation of the case for trial. So I understand that the parties will be contacted in order to make arrangements to meet with Mrs. Featherstone, the senior legal officer to this Trial Chamber III, at a Rule 65 ter conference in the near future. If there is nothing more to raise at this moment, -- Mr. Sainovic and Mr. Ojdanic, are there anything to raise for yourself at this moment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SAINOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED OJDANIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then this conference is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: adjourned at 3.22 p.m.
